I've recently posted this to our counterparts at Reddit, but I understand that some of us left and will never go back. I'm in that transition, myself. So for the benefit of those who missed it, I give you this interpretation of Phantom Limb. These are only my opinions, but I hope to spark some conversation here today.

It was discovered in "Pomp and Circuitry," and later reconfirmed by The Action Man in "All This and Gargantua 2," that a young Hamilton Fantomas was a member of Jonas Venture's Boys' Brigade. The nature of the Boys' Brigade is uncertain, but given the inclusion of Richard Impossible, we can reasonably assume it may have been a collection of scientists. With the exception of Jonas, himself, there weren't any scientists in Team Venture. Colonel Gentleman was a gentleman spy, Action Man was a super-soldier, Otto Aquarius is a half man/half mermaid abomination, Kano is a master of the martial arts and origami, Ook-Ook was a neanderthal (not a monkey,) and Swifty was a middleweight prize fighter.

The exception being Dr. Entmann/Humongaloid. Given the "doctor" prefix we can assume some background in science, and I personally believe the accident that caused his gigantism was a result of experimenting on himself. And let's be realistic. The man's tongue was too big for his mouth. I don't think he was doing too much sciencing during his time in Team Venture. Or at least, not until he shrunk, and even then, not for very much longer.

Team Venture, it seems, was originally comprised of individuals who befriended Jonas on his many adventures around the world; whereas, the Boy's Brigade seems to be made up of Jonas' scientific peers. Richard Impossible may have been along to document the capture of Spider-Skull Island, but he certainly didn't participate in the fracas (that accident must not have happened yet).

Fantomas, it seems, would have been a perfect attraction to the Boys' Brigade. He would've needed to excel in several areas of super-science. Robotics, cybernetics, biology, medicine, atomic physics, and I believe he was teaching a class on particle physics in "The Invisible Hand of Fate."

Kessler, chapter four...

I believe this to have been Karl G. Kessler,  who served as president in the (then) Optical Society of America. The OSA (now just "The Optical Society") focuses on optics and photonics.

Fantomas dedicated his life to science, as it seems it was the only way to go given nature was so unkind. And he had to excel, because it would have been the only way for State University to grant him such leeway for his own work.

In the late 80's, the OSI, or at least Brock and Hunter, believed Fantomas was a recruiter for the Guild of Calamitous Intent, but I don't believe this was the case. I'm inclined to believe that Fantomas was more inclined to take on students who were disenfranchised as he was. Or perhaps it was the students' own personal drives to be normal that led them to take such high-level courses. It's also possible that the students were placed in those courses by actual Guild recruiters.

I believe that Stevie's suicide was just that, suicide. The "pressure" that he couldn't take any longer I believe to be from the OSI. There was no evidence that Fantomas was doing anything wrong except for having an affair with the future Dr. Mrs. The Monarch. And there might not have been any evidence of that either. He would have needed to be extra discreet. In a deleted scene from "The Invisible Hand of Fate," it was revealed that Richard Impossible had been released from State University for having an affair with his future ex-wife, Sally.

I don't believe that Fantomas was knowingly working for the Guild, let alone actively recruiting for them. It's demonstrated in "All This and Gargantua 2" that the Guild throws money at legitimate protagonist scientists. Perhaps in an effort to cause havoc, perhaps in an effort to create horrible mutations and, thus, a new generation of supervillains.

They would have accomplished both goals with the Fantomas Machine, and a little help from the OSI. Fantomas chose Billy to be his lab assistant based solely on his paper. The one that Brock and Hunter had Stephen Hawking write. If not for this, then it's possible that none of the events of the series would have happened. Brock would never have been assigned to Dr. Venture. That assignment was always seen as "rookie work" or even as much as a punishment.

The Monarch would never have met his wife. Look at how lost The Monarch was in Season 2. Or his old costumes in "Shadowman 9 in the Cradle of Destiny." The Monarch would not be the man he is today without her, save for his hatred of Dr. Venture.

Also look at Fantomas' views on evil in "Shadowman 9."

Society slaps our wrists and tells us to simmer down, while she wages her murderous wars, destroys our planet, and prays to the mighty dollar

 If his experiment worked, I think we can reasonably assume that he would have worked towards things like world peace and economic prosperity. But he was twisted into the man he is, I feel, by Brock and Hunter.

Look no further than "Hate Floats," when he talks to Brock about the experiment that "made [him] evil." Fantomas, from birth, was shunned by a cruel and unforgiving world until the day that the invisible hand of fate, in its caprice, gifted him the tools needed to take revenge.

But if that day never happened, we wouldn't have the show that we all know and love.
